neighbours.label: A measure noun that heads a quantity phrase and is about to be followed by 'of' (the body's levels of sodium, a large amount of protein, enormous numbers of eggs, high concentrations of lead): the quantity word itself, not the substance measured
fire: Divers must watch the body's levels of nitrogen during a long ascent.
Volcanic eruptions release huge amounts of sulphur dioxide into the stratosphere.
The lagoon supports vast numbers of flamingos every winter.
Blood tests showed high concentrations of lead in the children's blood.
The reactor consumes small quantities of enriched uranium each year.
Only a tiny fraction of the seeds survive the first winter.
Fever raises the body's production of white blood cells.
The storm dumped record volumes of rain on the coastal towns.

predictions: Sentences with 'levels/amounts/numbers/concentrations/quantities/fraction/production/volumes of X' peak on that noun at 0.2-0.6. The same sentences with the substance named directly (release sulphur dioxide, supports flamingos) stay under 0.05.
notes: Probe: 'a large amount of protein' 0.536 (' amount'), "the body's levels of sodium" 0.527 (' levels'), 'enormous numbers of eggs' 0.341, 'sufficient quantities of reserves' 0.210, "the body's release of" 0.199; the same sentences without the measure noun 0.010-0.031.
